Merathaim
mer-ah-THAY-im
proper noun
Hebrew Merathayim, “double rebellion” or “double bitterness,” a symbolic name for Babylon in Jeremiah’s oracle of judgment.

📖 Biblical Definition

Merathaim is not so much a place as a verdict. In Jeremiah’s great prophecy against Babylon, the LORD summons the destroyer against the land under a name that spells out its guilt: “Go up against the land of Merathaim, even against it, and against the inhabitants of Pekod: waste and utterly destroy after them, saith the LORD” (Jer 50:21). The name means “double rebellion,” and it fastens upon Babylon the twofold charge of pride against God and cruelty against His people. The whole oracle is set against the golden city: “The word that the LORD spake against Babylon and against the land of the Chaldeans by Jeremiah the prophet” (Jer 50:1). His people are called out of her before the blow falls: “Flee out of the midst of Babylon, and deliver every man his soul” (Jer 51:6). And the New Testament takes up the same cry over the final Babylon: “Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen” (Rev 18:2). Merathaim teaches that God names sin truly and judges it exactly. The empire that flattered itself as eternal was, in heaven’s ledger, simply Double-Rebellion, ripe for the sword. Every proud power that rebels against God and oppresses His church wears the same name in His sight, and the same doom awaits it. The LORD does the naming, and His naming is the sentence.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A symbolic name for Babylon meaning “double rebellion” (Jer 50:21); heaven’s true verdict upon the proud empire ripe for judgment.

Jer 50:21 — "Go up against the land of Merathaim, even against it, and against the inhabitants of Pekod: waste and utterly destroy after them, saith the LORD,"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The symbolic name for Babylon, “double rebellion”; the entry recovers that God names sin truly and judges the proud empire exactly.

expand to see more

Merathaim strips the disguise from Babylon. The city called herself the golden queen of kingdoms; heaven called her Double-Rebellion. The name is the corruption named: pride against God and bitterness against His people, doubled and full. God does not flatter the powerful; He weighs them and writes their true name in His book.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the truthful judgment of God, who calls sin by its right name however the world gilds it. Empires and idols and ideologies present themselves in glittering titles; the LORD sees Merathaim, double rebellion, and appoints the sword. His people are commanded to come out of Babylon and not share her iniquity or her plagues. The final Babylon falls as the first did, and the same voice that named Merathaim cries, Babylon the great is fallen. God’s naming is His sentence, and His sentence is sure.
